note: The shared observable vocabulary. Each entry is checked against schemas/observable.schema.json. capabilities/*.json declare which configurations can produce which id, and the bridge resolves answerability against both.
why_open: plan.md 1 leaves the measured subject open on purpose, so this list cannot be enumerated in advance. What is fixed is the shape an entry must have. The list grows one entry at a time, when a question needs one. Settled on 2026-09-19: the list is deliberately never finished, so an experiment nobody anticipated can still be taken. This is the conclusion, not a pending decision.
rules: An entry is added when a question needs it, never speculatively. An unused vocabulary entry is a definition nobody has tested against data.

The estimator is part of the identity. Two sides agreeing on a word while disagreeing on how the number is extracted is worse than disagreeing openly: the values get compared and the discrepancy has no visible cause.

If the value depends on a lag, a window or an interval, window_required is true and the plan must carry that window as a condition. A window-dependent quantity is not one number, and recording it as one is how a short-lag and a long-lag result end up in the same column.
comparable is false until the same estimator demonstrably runs on both sides. Claiming it early makes a bridge round trip compare two different quantities under one name.

An id is never redefined, and adding is cheap while changing is not. A new id reinterprets nothing. But plans and results already cite the old one (P9), and a card carries the name only and reads the definition from here (5.1) -- so editing an entry silently changes what every card that already used that name meant, with no trace. definition, estimator and window_parameter are therefore append-only: correct them by standing a new id with supersedes and leaving the old one readable. units, producible_by, comparable and note may be edited in place, because none of them changes what a past number meant.

observables.definition: The short-time translational self-diffusion coefficient of dilute spherical tracers in the sample: the proportionality between mean squared displacement and lag time in the free regime, before hindrance by walls or by neighbouring particles sets in.
observables.estimator: Weighted least-squares fit of the mean squared displacement of single-particle positions against lag time, with the intercept left free so that localisation error stays out of the slope. D = slope / (2 * spatial_dimensions). Fit range: lags from one save interval up to max_lag_time, which must satisfy both bounds -- below the diffusive time tau_d, so the tracer is still free, and short enough against the record that every lag in the fit is determined. The plan declares the value and shows both. Weighting: by the number of independent displacements at each lag. A record of length T yields about T/tau of them at lag tau, so the variance of the MSD estimate grows sharply with lag, and equal weights hand the slope to the points that have the fewest samples. This is not a refinement: measured on the simulation side, equal weights over whole-record lags gave a 7 percent bias at 0.16 percent relative standard error -- a number that looks precise and is wrong, which is the failure a shared estimator exists to prevent.
observables.note: The first entry, and not a speculative seed: the M0 round trip, the bridge's r1_ask_simulation and six rejected/ cards already cite this name. comparable stays false until the same estimator has demonstrably run on both sides (rule 4). The estimator is written to be identical on both; the only difference is where the positions come from, tracked centroids on the microscope and trajectory frames in the engine. The fit range and the weighting were left open in the first version and are pinned here, because two sides can both fit 'the MSD below tau_d' and differ by more than the error either one reports.

observables.definition: The in-plane distribution of a trapped particle's centre about the trap. The scalar reported is the per-axis standard deviation of that position relative to the trap centre; the full histogram stays with the raw data.
observables.estimator: Track the particle centre in every frame, take the mean position as the trap centre and subtract it, and report the per-axis standard deviation over the declared record length. A particle counts as trapped when the distribution stays bounded about that centre for the whole record; drifting away is not trapped.
observables.note:
Deliberately the width and not the stiffness. sigma^2 = k_BT/k assumes a harmonic trap, and that assumption is not confirmed here -- sigma is measured without it, and a stiffness can be derived later with the assumption written down (P15). Whether the particle is trapped at all is not a separate observable but this distribution's success criterion: bounded or not. window_required is true because sigma converges from below: a short record undersamples the tails and understates it, and exposure-time averaging shaves it again, so a sigma written without its window is not one number.

COMPLEMENT: `trapped_particle_drag_offset` is the mean this estimator subtracts. Under a steady relative flow that mean is the whole signal, so a question about drag calibration needs that id and not this one (2026-09-23).

observables.definition: The detected signal rate of a single tracer under stated illumination and exposure: what one particle contributes to a frame, separated from background. Registered so a pre-measurement has an observable to name; it is the input six abstentions across A1 and A3 are waiting on.
observables.estimator: Segment single, well-separated tracers in each frame, integrate the signal over a fixed aperture around each centroid, subtract a local background estimated from an annulus outside it, and divide by the exposure time to give a rate. Report the median over particles and frames within the window, with the inter-particle spread, because the distribution over particles is what A1's detection limit needs and a mean hides it. Particles within one aperture diameter of another are excluded rather than deblended.
observables.note: One side only, which the schema allows and the bridge honours by refusing to ask the other for it. A simulation does not have a dye, a lot or a camera, so there is nothing on that side to compare against -- this is not a gap in the vocabulary but the fact that made the person rule this closes by acquiring.

observables.definition: The decay constant of tracer signal under continuous illumination at a stated setting. Produced by the same acquisition as tracer_brightness and registered with it.
observables.estimator: Take the per-particle brightness trace over the record using the tracer_brightness estimator frame by frame, and fit a single exponential in time to the population median. Report the decay constant with its fit spread and the illumination it was taken at. A single exponential is declared BEFORE the run and is not chosen after seeing the curve; if the residual shows it is wrong, that is a result and the criterion is not swapped for a better-fitting one.
observables.note: The illumination setting is part of the value and not context: the same particles bleach faster under more light. A rate reported without it cannot be carried to another plan.

observables.definition: The time a two-dimensional suspension of repulsive particles takes to reach its ordered steady state from a random initial configuration, read off the bond-orientational order parameter psi6. It is a property of the relaxation from a stated initial condition and not of the steady state it reaches.
observables.estimator: Compute psi6 per particle from its neighbours by Voronoi or a stated cutoff, average over particles to a single psi6(t), and report the time at which psi6(t) first reaches a DECLARED FRACTION of its plateau value, fitted over a declared lag window. The plateau fraction and the fit window are both conditions the plan must carry.
observables.note:
ONE id and not two, decided 2026-09-23. A driven question (a particle dragged through the same suspension) measures the same psi6 plateau by the same estimator, so it is this quantity at the conditions `driving_velocity` and `driving_direction`, with the undriven case as the v=0 row -- rule 2, the estimator is the identity. A proposed second id `driven_tracer_relaxation_time` was withdrawn on that ground. A second id becomes owed only if a driven question measures something psi6 does not define, such as a wake recovery time.

LIMITATION, recorded rather than hidden: TWO knobs move this number -- the plateau fraction and the fit window -- and `window_parameter` in observable.schema.json is a single string. The field names the fit window and the estimator above carries the plateau fraction as a declared condition. Nothing checks the second one the way check 40 checks the first.

observables.definition: The ensemble- and time-origin-averaged squared displacement of a particle centre as a function of lag time. The reported object is the curve on a declared lag grid; a single number is never this quantity.
observables.estimator: Unwrapped coordinates, so periodic images do not truncate the displacement. Average over particles and over time origins on a DECLARED lag grid. Overlapping time origins are NOT independent samples and an uncertainty that treats them as such is wrong; the count of independent origins is a declared condition. Report the curve, not a fitted scalar -- quantities derived from it are separate ids.
observables.note: The most dangerous name in this file, which is why it is registered before the questions that need it rather than after. Two questions can use this word for different lag grids and different averaging and never notice, because unlike `effective_translational_diffusivity` there is no adjective to warn a reader. `tracer_diffusivity` already paid this tuition once: uniform weighting across its whole range biased it 7 per cent while the reported error was 0.16 per cent.

observables.definition: The long-time translational diffusivity of a persistently self-propelled particle: the plateau of MSD/(2*d*t) once the motion has lost memory of its orientation. NOT the bare translational diffusivity D_T, which is the same curve read at short lag.
observables.estimator: Fit the slope of the mean squared displacement against lag time over a range whose LOWER bound lies well above the persistence time, and divide by 2*d. The lower bound is the condition that matters and it is the opposite direction from `tracer_diffusivity`, whose window is an UPPER bound protecting the free regime. A value read too early is D_T under this name.
observables.note: ONE id across two seats, decided 2026-09-23. Window 4 proposed `effective_diffusivity` and window 3 proposed this string for the same estimator -- same estimator, one id (rule 2), and the longer string wins because an active-matter question carries a rotational diffusivity in the same card and `effective_diffusivity` does not say which. `open_collisions` in quantities.json already records that this family's danger is a name that looks like its neighbours while being a different claim.

observables.definition: The local slope of log(MSD) against log(lag) over a declared lag range. Two for ballistic motion, one for diffusive, and the value between them is what a crossover looks like.
observables.estimator: Least-squares slope of log(MSD) on log(lag) over a DECLARED lag range. Short-time and long-time slopes are this one quantity at two windows, not two quantities. Distinguish in the plan whether MSD/(2*d*t) or the local derivative d(MSD)/dt/(2*d) underlies the curve being differentiated: the two differ by exactly the amount this slope is measuring.
observables.note: Stands in place of a proposed `time_resolved_effective_diffusivity`. D_eff(t) is a curve, and this file's convention is that an entry names the SCALAR reported while the full object stays with the raw data -- `trapped_position_distribution` reports a standard deviation and keeps its histogram. Registering the curve as an observable would have had to collapse it to a scalar somewhere, and collapsing it is what deletes the question.

observables.definition: The decay time of a self-propelled particle's orientational autocorrelation, MEASURED from the trajectory. Not 1/((d-1)*D_R), which is the same number only when the model holds exactly.
observables.estimator: Fit an exponential to the autocorrelation of the orientation unit vector over a declared lag window and report its decay time.
observables.note: Deliberately the fitted one. Both seats offered the analytic alternative and both noted it restates the input: a formula on declared inputs measures nothing and cannot disagree with the model, so it is not an observable at all. If the derived number is needed it belongs in quantities.json as a derived quantity with the formula's own grade.

observables.definition: The distance over which a self-propelled particle keeps its direction, MEASURED from the crossover in its mean squared displacement.
observables.estimator: Fit the ballistic-to-diffusive crossover of the mean squared displacement over a declared lag window and report the length scale at which it occurs.
observables.note: Same choice and same reason as `persistence_time`: v0 * persistence_time is a formula on inputs and measures nothing. Keeping the fitted one is what lets the two disagree, and a disagreement is the only thing either could have told us.

observables.definition: The lag at which a mean squared displacement stops being ballistic and starts being diffusive, defined by its log-log slope passing a stated value between 2 and 1.
observables.estimator: Take `msd_loglog_slope` on a rolling lag window and report the lag at which it first crosses a DECLARED threshold between 2 and 1. The threshold is the window: 1.5 and 1.1 give different numbers from one run.
observables.note: Reads off the same curve as `msd_loglog_slope` and is a separate id because the reported scalar is a time, not a slope.

observables.definition: The steady-state MEAN displacement of a trapped particle from its trap centre along the flow axis, while the surrounding fluid moves at constant velocity relative to the trap. The trap centre here is the geometric centre of the confining potential and not the time-averaged particle position.
observables.estimator: Track the particle centre over a declared record length under steady flow and report the mean displacement from the DECLARED trap centre, resolved along the flow direction. The record length is the window: the standard error of a mean falls as sqrt(1/T), so a displacement quoted without it is not one number.
observables.note: THE COMPLEMENT OF `trapped_position_distribution`, READ FROM THE SAME TRACE, and the two must be read together. That entry takes the MEAN POSITION AS THE TRAP CENTRE AND SUBTRACTS IT before reporting a standard deviation -- the quantity it discards is this one, exactly and not approximately. A reader who reaches for the registered name to answer a drag-calibration question computes the one number that cannot answer it. Raised by the execution seat that hit it, 2026-09-23.
